note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection without signs or signals, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Which practices help drive safely at night?
options: a:Only drive if you are tired,b:Turn off headlights in rural areas to see better.,c:Increase your following distance and ensure headlights are working.
note: At night, increase following distance, avoid driving while fatigued, and keep headlights in proper working order to maximize visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left and oncoming traffic is heavy while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Remain in the intersection only if necessary and safe, or use the next intersection if needed.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear before entering the intersection.,c:Enter and wait in the center of the intersection until traffic clears.
note: You may enter the intersection to prepare for a left turn on a green light if it is safe, but do not block traffic—use the next intersection if necessary.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings in general?
options: a:Safe to cross since trains are rare.,b:As potentially dangerous and requiring caution.,c:Safe places to park.
note: Treat all railroad crossings as hazardous; look and listen for trains and obey all posted signals and gates.

question: What does a broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means drivers on the side next to the broken line may pass when it is safe; drivers next to the solid line may not.

question: Signs that are orange in color normally indicate:
options: a:Regulatory rules such as speed limits.,b:School zones only.,c:Work zones and temporary traffic control.
note: Orange signs are used in highway work zones to warn drivers of construction or maintenance activities.

question: Which device is commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road only.,b:Flashing red lights on the shoulder.,c:Arrows painted on lanes and overhead lane-control arrows.
note: Arrows (painted or on overhead signals) direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp properly?
options: a:Keep the same speed while on the ramp.,b:Do not slow down until you have moved onto the exit ramp,c:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
note: Maintain highway speed until you begin the ramp, then decelerate in the ramp's designated deceleration lane.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:On a hill under any circumstances.,b:Anywhere inside a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is illegal to park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes; when parking on the street, stay within 12 inches of the curb.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving normally until you reach your destination.,b:Slam on your brakes immediately.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop off the road.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and safely pull off the road before braking heavily.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open a window to stay awake.,b:Drink coffee and keep going.,c:Stop driving and rest.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; the safest choice is to stop and rest.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warning of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:School zones only.,c:Public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn drivers of potential hazards or conditions that require caution.

question: What single action most reduces your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt is the most effective way to reduce injury or death in a crash.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be protected?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult.,b:They must be properly restrained in appropriate child seats or safety belts.,c:They can stand on the floor in the back seat if supervised.
note: Children must be secured in suitable child safety seats or seat belts; no adult can reliably hold a child during a crash.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is allowed.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: A broken yellow center line separates opposite-direction traffic and indicates passing is permitted when safe.

question: Which behavior is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than traffic at all times.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Signaling correctly when changing lanes.
note: Signs of intoxicated driving include weaving, speeding or driving unusually slowly, sudden stops, and jerking motions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Only to vehicles that have a green arrow.,b:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Only to the driver on your right.
note: When turning left yield to oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists who have the right-of-way.

question: At a railroad crossing, how far must you stop from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing?
options: a:Can drive around a lowered gate if no train is coming.,b:Must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning lights are flashing.,c:Must stop at least 10 feet from the nearest rail.
note: When active warning devices operate, stop well back (at least 15 feet) from the nearest rail and never go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,b:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only in rural areas.
note: Driving unnecessarily slowly so that traffic is disrupted is illegal; you may be required to pull over and let vehicles pass.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying hazardous situations and acting to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of other drivers to avoid problems.,c:Following the vehicle ahead closely to observe its actions.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking steps to avoid crashes by adjusting your actions early.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance in situations that reduce visibility or stopping ability — behind large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, or when tailgated.

question: If another vehicle is about to hit you, what is an appropriate immediate action?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:Wave your arms frantically.,c:Only use emergency lights.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians when you believe they may not see you and a collision is imminent.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline?
options: a:Single broken yellow,b:Combination broken and solid yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: Double solid yellow centerlines prohibit passing from either direction.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Eating,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.
note: Using a phone to read or send texts, as well as other tasks like eating or adjusting devices, distracts you from driving.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or historic sites?
options: a:Brown.,b:Green.,c:Orange.
note: Brown signs designate public recreation, cultural, or historic areas and sites.

question: Which of these effects does alcohol NOT cause?
options: a:It distorts judgment of speed and distance.,b:It makes you more alert.,c:It slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, distorts distance/speed judgment, reduces alertness, and increases risky behavior.

question: At a light rail crossing, what must drivers always do?
options: a:Obey traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates if safe.,c:Assume trains will yield to vehicles.
note: Never drive around lowered gates. Always obey signs and signals and look both ways before crossing rail tracks.

question: Why is extra alertness required around motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and harder to see, often hidden in blind spots.,b:They rarely use lights at night.,c:Motorcyclists are generally less skilled than car drivers.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots; their speed and distance are harder to judge, so use extra caution near them.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Are only found in construction zones.,b:Provide information and guide drivers.,c:Are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings give drivers information about lane use, safe passing zones, and upcoming road conditions to help position vehicles and drive safely.

question: Why should you exercise extra caution when near snowplows?
options: a:They usually drive faster than other vehicles.,b:They are typically narrower than most vehicles.,c:They often reduce visibility by creating clouds of blowing snow.
note: Snowplows are wider and slower than most vehicles and can create blowing snow that greatly reduces visibility, so give them extra space.

question: What should you do when the road is slippery from rain, snow, or ice?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously than normal.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
note: Reduce speed and avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery surfaces; do not use cruise control in such conditions.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield the right-of-way: move to the side and stop if necessary so the emergency vehicle can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.,c:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
note: Do not back up or turn around on the highway; go to the next exit and use that to safely return.

question: At night, when another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction, your headlights should be:
options: a:Off — use parking lights instead.,b:Set to high beam.,c:Set to low beam.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle; switch to low beam to avoid blinding other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are on a divided multilane highway and hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at the same speed and let it pass.,b:Slow down,c:Disregard the signal if other lanes are open.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren you must give a clear path—slow down, move over, and stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way intersection controlled by stop signs, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who signals first.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at stop signs, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: a:Wearing a safety belt helps a driver maintain control of their vehicle.,b:A child safety seat should never be placed in front of an active airbag.,c:Only persons under the age of 18 are required to wear a seat belt.
note: Vermont law requires all vehicle occupants to be properly restrained; the statement that only persons under 18 must wear seat belts is false.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.,c:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe.

question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Only large vehicles inside the roundabout.,b:Vehicles,c:Only pedestrians.
note: Yield to traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the roundabout before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm is extended downward, what does that hand signal indicate?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: Left arm pointing down is the hand signal for slowing or stopping; follow accordingly if you are behind that vehicle.

question: How should you drive when passing through a work zone?
options: a:Keep a two-second following distance behind any vehicle ahead of you.,b:Slow down and pay attention.,c:Closely follow the vehicle ahead to clear the zone quickly.
note: Slow down, pay attention to signs and workers, maintain a safe following distance (about four seconds), and avoid lane changes where workers are present.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,b:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,c:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
note: Strong emotions and stress reduce concentration and decision-making ability; avoid driving while emotionally unsettled.

question: What does a green traffic arrow mean when displayed for a lane?
options: a:It allows you to proceed in any direction.,b:It is used only on one-way streets.,c:It functions like a circular green light
note: A green arrow means traffic in the indicated lane may proceed, but only in the direction shown by the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It means drivers may turn in the arrow direction without yielding.,b:It is never used.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — slow and prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected-turn signal is ending; slow and prepare to stop unless it is unsafe to do so.

question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating vehicles traveling 25 mph or less.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:The exact safe speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,c:Only a suggested speed.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive more slowly when conditions are poor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When on a narrow road and meeting an oncoming vehicle, what should you allow?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.
note: On narrow roads both drivers should allow sufficient roadway—about one-half of the main-traveled portion—so both can pass safely.

question: In which situations is it important to slow down?
options: a:At intersections or railroad crossings.,b:When the road is wet or slippery.,c:On narrow or winding roads.
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills and sharp curves, and when roads are slippery.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different highways, which driver must yield?
options: a:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,b:Either driver depending on who signals first.,c:The driver on the right must yield to the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do about following distance?
options: a:Decrease their following distance.,b:Increase their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach their destination faster.
note: When roads are wet, icy, or visibility is reduced, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead to allow more time to react.

question: Which of these is an effect of alcohol on drivers?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination even at low levels of consumption.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a red light and a green arrow at the same time, what does it allow?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light before proceeding in any direction.,b:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow.,c:You may proceed only straight ahead.
note: When a green arrow is displayed with a red light, drivers may go only in the direction of the arrow and only if the intersection is clear.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, how should you handle driving?
options: a:You will drive no differently than you would if you were calm.,b:Take the time to calm and focus before starting the engine.,c:You can drive faster because you are more alert.
note: Emotional distress impairs concentration; calm down and regain focus before driving to avoid putting yourself and others at risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it lawful to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement.,c:When the other vehicle is waiting or turning left and there is a safe available lane on the right.
note: Passing on the right is permitted on multi-lane roads or when the vehicle ahead is turning left and a safe right lane exists; never pass off pavement or on narrow bridges.

question: When is it necessary to look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when preparing to park.,b:Only when turning right.,c:When changing lanes or otherwise moving your vehicle laterally (e.g.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them) in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: Before changing lanes, what should you make sure to do?
options: a:Only rely on your mirrors.,b:Check side and rearview mirrors,c:Only check for oncoming traffic ahead.
note: Before a lane change, check mirrors, signal well in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas), and glance over your shoulder for blind spot vehicles.

question: Which commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving and excessive speed for conditions as well as following too closely.,b:Only bad weather.,c:Mechanical failures exclusively.
note: Common causes include inattention, driving too fast for conditions, and tailgating; all increase crash risk.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and then driving?
options: a:Acceptable after only a couple of drinks.,b:A minor issue if you feel sober.,c:A serious traffic safety problem that makes safe driving impossible.
note: Driving after drinking is extremely dangerous; alcohol impairs the skills required for safe driving.

question: How should a seat belt fit when adjusted properly?
options: a:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,b:Is hidden beneath the seat.,c:Is loose.
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should rest across the chest.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Always when pedestrians are in the street, even if they cross carelessly.,b:Only if the pedestrian is using a crosswalk.,c:Only if they are on the same side of the street as the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway regardless of how or where they cross; exercise caution and yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb mandatory?
options: a:You need only signal during the maneuver itself.,b:Yes — signaling is required by law and is a good driving habit.,c:No — signal only if other traffic is present.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; always signal before pulling away from a curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down at the light.,b:Stop,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and proceeding only when the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed slowly and ignore it if possible.,b:Stop immediately in your current lane.,c:Drive as far right as is safe and stop.
note: On two-lane or undivided highways, pull as far right as possible and stop, taking care not to block intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway, you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Drive slowly on the entrance ramp so you can check traffic.
note: When merging into freeway traffic, use the acceleration lane to match speed, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lie down and sleep in the car.
note: Remain in your vehicle — you're more likely to be found and it's safer than venturing out in a storm.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,b:Slow down and proceed if the way looks clear.,c:Creep forward into the intersection and wait.
note: A red arrow means you must come to a full stop and remain stopped until a green signal or arrow allows you to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: By law, how far before a turn or lane change must you signal?
options: a:100 feet or about three to five seconds in normal driving.,b:10 feet,before turning.,c:50 feet before the turn.,d:30 feet before the turn.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before a turn or lane change; signaling three to five seconds in advance is a good rule.

question: When you enter a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
options: a:Your seat so you can reach the controls and see the road clearly.,b:The steering wheel, then the seat.,c:Only your rearview mirror.
note: Adjust your seat first to ensure you can reach pedals and controls comfortably, then adjust mirrors and steering wheel as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield,c:When you see flashing lights or hear a siren.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens by pulling over to provide a clear path and stopping if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-way road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Only after signaling for at least five seconds.,b:Immediately after passing the vehicle's rear bumper.,c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
note: Return to your lane only when there is sufficient space between you and the passed vehicle to do so safely.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas.,b:Do not immediately use your brakes; gradually slow down and pull off the road.,c:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, avoid hard braking until under control, then slow and pull over safely.

question: If you notice a defect that may affect safe operation of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can get it fixed.,c:Correct the defect when you can afford it.
note: Any defect that could affect safe operation should be repaired promptly before driving the vehicle under normal conditions.

question: What are the rights and responsibilities of bicyclists on most roads?
options: a:They may not ride on public roads.,b:They have fewer rules to follow than motorists.,c:They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle operators.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles, including following traffic laws and signaling turns.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction times.,b:It makes you more alert.,c:It improves concentration.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reducing reaction time and impairing judgement needed for safe driving.

question: If an emergency vehicle is directly behind you in heavy traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Keep moving slowly until you can safely pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: If you cannot immediately pull over because of traffic, keep moving slowly and clear a path as soon as you can to let it pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert others.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,c:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
note: When entering from a private road or driveway you must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The largest vehicle has the right‑of‑way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the center of the road ahead.,c:Over the shoulder.
note: If oncoming headlights blind you, keep your eyes toward the right side of the road ahead and avoid looking directly at the lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parked uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your steering wheel?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead and release the parking brake.,b:Turn the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll into the curb; always set the parking brake.

question: In most fatal crashes involving a large truck and a passenger vehicle, who is responsible for causing the crash?
options: a:Poor weather.,b:The driver of the passenger vehicle.,c:The truck driver.
note: In the majority of fatal crashes involving trucks and passenger vehicles, the passenger vehicle driver, not the truck driver, was the one who caused the crash.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Stay seated and wait for help without turning on hazards.,b:Sound your horn to alert passing drivers.,c:Signal and carefully exit the roadway
note: Safely get your vehicle off the traveled roadway, turn on hazard flashers, and lift the hood to signal a disabled vehicle.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Do not affect driving abilities.,c:Are distracting activities.
note: Smoking while driving diverts hands and eyes from driving and can create dangerous distractions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these has priority if there is a conflict: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: An authorized traffic officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot when moving left, where should you glance?
options: a:Only at the side mirror.,b:Over your right shoulder.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: To verify the left blind spot is clear, glance over your left shoulder in the direction you intend to move.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
options: a:No blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have bigger blind spots; avoid lingering alongside or directly behind where the driver cannot see you.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Engage four‑wheel drive and maintain normal speeds.,b:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
note: On snow- or ice-covered roads, reduce your speed and increase following distance; these are the most important techniques to avoid crashes.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They are better drivers because they are more cautious.,b:They are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time; never drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Reduce your speed significantly.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots to ensure no one is trying to pass you.
note: Look in mirrors and over your shoulder to check blind spots; ensure no one is passing before switching lanes.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Overcorrect sharply in the opposite direction.,b:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.,c:Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
note: When a vehicle skids, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid until you regain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can fully pass through it.,b:Move forward until the traffic clears even if you partially block the intersection.,c:Get close to the car in front of you to keep traffic moving.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking intersections disrupts traffic flow and can be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, what should you do when an emergency vehicle with lights approaches?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Turn on your flashers and proceed.,c:Speed up and exit the street quickly.
note: On a one-way street you should pull to the nearest roadside and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb (to the left).,c:Keep the wheels straight and set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will move away from traffic.

question: Which of the following is true about using headlights?
options: a:Driving while using low beam headlights during the daytime can reduce the risk of head-on collisions.,b:Headlights are required only during daytime.,c:When snow
note: Use headlights from a half-hour after sunset until a half-hour before sunrise, and anytime visibility is reduced by weather.

question: Which is true about passing a motorcycle?
options: a:It is acceptable to pass a motorcycle without changing lanes if space is tight.,b:Motorcycles are entitled to less lane width than other vehicles.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; change lanes completely when passing to give them sufficient space.

question: Which action best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check behind it before you get into the driver's seat.,b:Check your rearview mirror from the driver's seat, then back up.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Backing requires extra caution; before getting into the vehicle to back up, walk behind it to check for children, pets, or objects.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: White pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your turn signals are not working, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Your horn.,b:Your headlights.,c:Hand signals.
note: When electronic signals fail, use standard hand signals to show your intention to turn or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver who is traveling much slower than the posted speed do when traffic backs up behind them?
options: a:Refuse to let following cars pass.,b:Always maintain the slower speed regardless of traffic.,c:Pull off the road at the first safe location and allow following vehicles to pass.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving excessively slowly, pull off safely and let vehicles pass.

question: Which of the following is a distracted-driving behavior?
options: a:Resting instead of driving while tired.,b:Leaving the house early to drive to an appointment.,c:Texting a message on your cell phone
note: Using a phone to read or send text messages while driving diverts your eyes and attention from the road and is illegal in many places.

question: When should parking lights be used?
options: a:Only when the vehicle is parked.,b:Only during winter driving.,c:When passing another vehicle.
note: Parking lights are intended for use only when the vehicle is parked.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.,b:Give yourself extra space when stopping.,c:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery just after rain begins; slow down, increase following distance, and avoid standing water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which is correct?
options: a:Turn wheels slightly right.,b:Turn wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: What headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to what lane space?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Half the width of a lane.,c:The bicycle lane.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to a full lane and should be given the same space as other vehicles.

question: Why is night driving more challenging than daytime driving?
options: a:Because it is more likely to rain at night.,b:Because visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Because cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced; use headlights and drive at speeds that allow you to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors.,b:Check your mirrors,c:Begin signaling only after you start moving into the next lane.
note: Before changing lanes, glance over your shoulder to check blind spots, use mirrors, and signal about 100 feet in advance in residential areas (longer on freeways).

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only if you see a train approaching at close range.,b:When flashing red signals and gates are operating or when directed by a flagger.,c:Only when there is a stop sign.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when signals or gates are active or when instructed by a flagger; always obey posted controls.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down.,b:Retaliate by tailgating them.,c:Avoid eye contact
note: Stay calm, avoid eye contact and gestures, and put distance between you and the aggressive driver by slowing and letting them pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,b:Signal,c:Always use cruise control.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to clear blind spots before changing lanes; cruise control is not appropriate in heavy traffic or poor conditions.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.,b:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,c:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.
note: Coffee or other stimulants do not reduce BAC or sober you up; only time metabolizes alcohol out of your system.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means what?
options: a:Slow down immediately.,b:Pass with caution at any time.,c:Do not pass from your direction.
note: If the solid yellow line is adjacent to your lane, passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: What is a common cause of many crashes?
options: a:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.,b:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,c:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
note: Driving too fast for conditions (even below the posted limit) is a frequent factor in crashes; adjust speed for weather and road conditions.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Opposite directions of travel.,b:Passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and you may change lanes when safe.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction; you may cross them to pass or change lanes when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal?
options: a:Slow and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Ignore it and proceed as you would on a green arrow.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Assume the tracks are clear if no train is visible.,b:Speed up to clear the crossing quickly.,c:Slow down
note: Slow, scan left and right for trains, and stop if signals or gates indicate an approaching train; never go around lowered gates.

question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene on the roadway?
options: a:Pull over,b:Always stop to view the scene.,c:Keep driving and stay attentive unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep your attention on driving and proceed safely.

question: What is the usual effect of driving while distracted?
options: a:It usually causes the driver to drive faster.,b:It causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:It never affects driving.
note: Distractions slow reaction time and increase crash risk; avoid activities that take attention from driving.
